raw_case_text:
A 47-year-old man presented with fever, headache, and myalgia for 7 days associated with vomiting and hematemesis of three episodes. He had reduced consciousness and suffered an episode of generalized tonic-clonic seizure on the day of the presentation. On initial assessment, his Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was E1V1M3 with unequal pupils of the right 3 mm and left 2 mm. The patient was hemodynamically stable with a pulse rate of 82, blood pressure of 148/87 mmHg and he was febrile with a temperature of 38.7 C. He was intubated and stabilized. Following that, his computed tomography (CT) brain revealed left thalamic bleed and right frontotemporoparietal acute subdural hemorrhage 30 mm in thickness with compression of adjacent brain parenchyma and the right lateral ventricle. There was midline shift of 20 mm to the left and effacement of basal cisterns [Figure 1].
The first blood tests on day 7 of fever recorded a total white cell count of 4.53 x 109/L, platelet count of 31 x 109/L, hematocrit 42.7%, and a lymphocyte count of 1.40 x 109/L. International normalized ratio (INR) was 2.63 with activated prothrombin time (APTT) 40.5 s. Nonstructural protein (NS1) antigen test was positive, dengue IgM negative and dengue IgG positive.
Coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia were treated with transfusion of fresh frozen plasma and platelet concentrate. The patient was sedated for cerebral resuscitation. The platelet count improved to 56 x 109/L and the INR reduced to 1.2 with APTT of 34.5 s. Unfortunately, the pupils were both dilated (5 mm) and were nonreactive prior to operation.
An operation was attempted 8 h after admission. A right decompressive craniectomy, evacuation of blood clots, external ventricular drainage catheter insertion, and fascia duraplasty was done.
Postoperatively, pupils remained 5 mm and nonreactive with GCS of E1VTM1 without sedation. There was no cough or gag reflex present. A repeat CT brain postoperation showed generalized cerebral edema with loss of grey-white matter differentiation, effacement of sulci and basal cisterns, bilateral thalamic bleeds, and midline shift of 10 mm to the right. Soon after, the patient's hemodynamic status deteriorated and required inotropic support. The patient died on the 3rd day of admission.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 47-year-old man presenting with a 7-day history of fever, headache, myalgia, vomiting, three episodes of hematemesis, acute seizure, and coma.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 47-year-old male presented with a 7-day history of fever, headache, and myalgia, complicated by recurrent vomiting and three episodes of hematemesis. On the day of admission, he experienced acute deterioration of consciousness and a generalized tonic-clonic seizure, prompting emergent hospital presentation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, headache, myalgia, vomiting, hematemesis, generalized seizure, and decreased consciousness. Medications and allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 38.7 C, pulse rate: 82 beats/min, blood pressure: 148/87 mmHg. GCS on arrival E1V1M3 (5/15), unequal pupils (right 3 mm, left 2 mm). Following intubation and resuscitation, both pupils dilated to 5 mm and became nonreactive. Postoperatively: GCS E1VTM1 without sedation, absent cough and gag reflexes.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC: 4.53 x 10^9/L, lymphocytes: 1.40 x 10^9/L, platelet count: 31 x 10^9/L (improved to 56 x 10^9/L post-transfusion), hematocrit: 42.7%. Coagulation: INR 2.63 (reduced to 1.2 post-plasma), aPTT 40.5 sec (reduced to 34.5 sec).
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT (preoperative): Right frontotemporoparietal acute subdural hematoma 30 mm in thickness with marked compression of adjacent brain parenchyma and right lateral ventricle, midline shift of 20 mm to the left, effacement of basal cisterns, and a left thalamic bleed. Brain CT (postoperative): Generalized cerebral edema with loss of grey-white differentiation, effacement of sulci and basal cisterns, bilateral thalamic hemorrhages, and persistent 10 mm midline shift.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe dengue hemorrhagic fever (secondary dengue) complicated by massive spontaneous acute subdural hematoma, bilateral thalamic hemorrhages, uncal herniation, and fatal cerebral edema. Diagnostic confirmation: Positive dengue virus nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) antigen; negative dengue IgM and positive dengue IgG, confirming acute secondary dengue infection.
Plan & Outcome: Emergent endotracheal intubation, cerebral resuscitation, and transfusion of fresh frozen plasma and platelet concentrates. Underwent emergency right decompressive craniectomy, clot evacuation, external ventricular drain insertion, and fascia duraplasty. Postoperatively, brainstem reflexes remained absent, hemodynamic collapse ensued requiring inotropic support, and the patient died on the 3rd hospital day.
